module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Group.Finset.Defs
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Archimedean.Real.Basic
public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic

@[expose] public section

namespace SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

/--
Fractional alpha. This is defined as
$$
\max_x \sum_{v \in V} x_v
$$
subject to $0 \le x_v \le 1$ for all $v \in V$ and
$x_u + x_v \le 1$ whenever $(u, v)$ are connected by an edge.
-/
noncomputable def fractionalAlpha (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : ℝ :=
  sSup {(∑ i, x i) | (x : α → ℝ) (_ : ∀ v, x v ∈ Set.Icc 0 1)
    (_ : ∀ u v, G.Adj u v → x u + x v ≤ 1)}


end SimpleGraph

reformulations.difference: The definition takes a real supremum of feasible objective values, whereas the docstring and MathWorld's equation (1) specify a maximum.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The zero assignment is feasible. The feasible assignments form a closed subset of the compact finite product [0,1]^V, and their sums lie between 0 and |V|. The continuous sum therefore attains its maximum, which equals the real supremum. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, alpha_eq_maximum_iff proves that fractionalAlpha G = a is equivalent to having a feasible assignment of sum a and every feasible assignment having sum at most a.

review.notes: Checked the file's sole declaration. It faithfully defines the documented edge-constrained fractional independence parameter. The clique-constrained fractional packing number in Acín et al. is a distinct notion, not an intended equivalent here. No Mathlib duplicate or downstream declaration use was found; the only external name occurrence is the module's aggregate import. Scratch proofs establish nonemptiness, boundedness, maximum attainment, independence from the adjacency-decidability instance, and agreement of 0/1 feasible assignments with Mathlib's IsIndepSet. Exact real-valued tests cover the empty graph, edgeless graphs, K1, K2, K3, and one edge plus an isolated vertex. Rational candidate enumeration returns the corresponding values [0, 1, 1, 3/2, 3, 2]. The final scratch compilation succeeds without sorry axioms. The reviewed file was not modified.
